reel.title: 2 Russian missiles crashed in Poland | Mistake or message?
reel.topic: Russian missiles and a drone came down in south-east Poland early on Friday 20 Nov, during Russia's overnight attack on Ukraine (Zelenskyy: more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic; at least eight civilians killed). AP: 'Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday.' Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz: 'two missiles and a jet-powered drone fell on Polish territory' (Al Jazeera). Sites: Nowy Lipowiec (a Kh-101 cruise missile, confirmed by prosecutors on Saturday: 'manufactured in the fourth quarter of this year', dpa), Rudnik nad Sanem (the ministry says a second missile; no final identification by midday on 21 Nov, Global Security Centre) and Mołodycz (most likely a jet-powered drone). No one was hurt. One missile is believed to have crashed about 35 km from the Koalicja 26.2 exercise at Nowa Dęba (AP): 2,800 soldiers from 11 countries, led by the UK and France (dpa), preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine (AP). Tusk: it appeared 'we are dealing with an intentional provocation'; 'This doesn't look like an accident.' Hours before, Trump had told Fox News: 'Putin has been landing drones in Poland and a couple of little missiles, by mistake.' Moscow: 'no immediate comment' (AP, Friday); 'Moscow had still not commented on the incident' (Global Security Centre, 21 Nov 12:00 CET); Russia's defence ministry said the sites it hit that night were linked to Ukraine's military. NATO: Rutte called it a 'grave violation'; in Warsaw on Saturday: 'I can guarantee that NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory' (dpa). Poland asked for AWACS aircraft and F-35s (RBC-Ukraine). The North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels on Monday 23 Nov, 'dedicated to the Russian missile violation of Polish airspace' (Poland's mission to NATO via Polskie Radio, in the Kyiv Post). Article 4 consultations 'had not been requested by 12:00' on 21 Nov (Global Security Centre).
